content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline bookmark-manager specification is ready for review.

- Spec: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all checklist items passed; no unresolved clarifications

The draft covers private accounts, saving/editing/deleting bookmarks, collections, tags, favorites, duplicate detection, search/filter/sort, responsive use, and clear first-release exclusions.

Please approve the specification or describe any changes. After approval, I’ll move to the implementation-plan gate. No code has been written yet.

Thanks for putting this together — it's clearly thorough, and a lot of it matches what I picture: saving links, editing and deleting them, tagging, favorites, the duplicate warning, searching and sorting, and it all working on my phone and laptop. That part reads right to me.

But reading it closely, a few things I really care about seem to be missing or not quite what I had in mind:

1. **Saving should do the heavy lifting for me.** When I paste a link, I don't just want it to guess a title — I want it to actually go grab the page's real title, its short description, the little site icon, and if possible a preview image, and fill those in for me automatically. I'd still want to be able to change any of that before or after saving. Right now it sounds like it only makes up a fallback title and deliberately doesn't reach out to the page, and that's not what I want.

2. **A "read it later" pile.** Separate from favorites, I want to flag links I haven't gotten to yet, and have a spot that shows me only those unread ones — and marking one as read takes it off that list. I don't see that here.

3. **Archiving, not just deleting.** Sometimes I'm done with a link but don't want to throw it away. I'd like to tuck it away so it's out of my main list and searches, but I can still go to an "archived" area and find it or bring it back. Delete should be the permanent one; archive should be the reversible one.

4. **Doing things to a bunch at once.** When I'm tidying up, I want to select several bookmarks and, say, tag them all, mark them read, archive them, or delete them in one go — including everything that matches whatever I'm currently filtered to.

5. **Smarter searching.** Beyond plain text, I'd like to search by tag directly (something like typing `#news`), combine terms with and/or/not, and search an exact phrase in quotes. And when I'm typing a tag onto a bookmark, it should suggest tags I already use.

6. **A longer note.** Besides the short description, I'd like a place to jot a fuller note on a bookmark with a bit of formatting, and see it nicely when I open the bookmark.

7. **Saving a search to reuse.** If I set up a search with certain tags included and excluded, I'd like to save that combination and jump back to it later.

One question on collections: the way you've written it, each bookmark sits in only one collection like a folder. I mostly think in tags, so I want to be sure tags stay the main way I organize and that a link can carry several. Collections on top of that are fine, but they shouldn't replace flexible tagging.

Could you fold these in and show me the updated version? A couple of things like importing/exporting from a browser I'm happy to leave for later, but the ones above matter to me for a first version.

content:
The specification has been updated and revalidated.

- Updated spec: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Validation: all checklist items pass; no unresolved clarifications

The first release now includes:

- Automatic title, description, site-icon, and preview-image retrieval
- Editable metadata plus longer formatted notes
- A separate Read Later/unread workflow
- Reversible archiving and distinct permanent deletion
- Individual selection and “select all matching” bulk actions
- `#tag`, quoted-phrase, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` searching
- Existing-tag suggestions
- Reusable saved searches
- Tags as the primary many-to-many organization model
- Optional, secondary single-collection placement

The Spec-Driven Development workflow keeps us at the specification approval gate. No implementation or planning has started. If this version matches your intent, approve it and I’ll prepare the implementation plan next.

This looks great — you've picked up everything I asked about. Reading through it:

- Pasting a link and having the title, description, site icon, and preview image pulled in automatically, with me able to change any of it — yes, that's exactly it, and I like that a slow or unreachable page still lets me save.
- The separate Read Later queue that's independent of favorites — right.
- Archiving that tucks things away reversibly, with delete staying the permanent one — good.
- Selecting several at once, or everything matching my current search, and acting on them all — yes.
- The richer search with `#tag`, exact phrases in quotes, and and/or/not — and tag suggestions as I type — good.
- The longer formatted note — good.
- Saving a search to come back to later — yes.
- Tags being the main way I organize with collections as an optional extra — that's the balance I wanted.

I'm happy with this version of the specification. Please go ahead and prepare the implementation plan.

One small note just so it isn't lost for later: down the road I'll want to bring in bookmarks I already have from my browser and get them back out again, and possibly keep a saved copy of a page's contents — but I'm fine leaving those out of this first version as you've noted.

Approved — go ahead to the planning step.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review.

- Plan: [plan.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- Technical decisions: [research.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- Data model: [data-model.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- HTTP API contract: [http-api.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/http-api.md)
- Search grammar: [search-syntax.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/search-syntax.md)
- Validation guide: [quickstart.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)
- Branch: `001-bookmark-manager`

The plan uses a single Node.js 24 LTS/Fastify service, React client, SQLite with FTS5, secure server-side metadata capture, and cached visual assets. These choices were checked against the official [Node.js lifecycle](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [Fastify documentation](https://fastify.dev/docs/v5.0.x/Guides/Migration-Guide-V5/), [SQLite FTS5 specification](https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html), and [OWASP SSRF guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html).

The `speckit-plan` workflow drove the supporting research, data model, contracts, and runnable acceptance guide. There are no unresolved technical clarifications or planning-gate violations.

Browser import/export and full-page snapshots remain documented extension points, excluded from v1 as agreed. No tasks or application code have been created yet. If you approve this plan, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks next.

This all sounds sensible to me. I can't speak to the technical choices in any depth, but what matters to me is that the plan carries through everything we settled on, and reading it that way I'm reassured:

- Automatic title/description/icon/preview capture that still lets me save when a page won't load — there.
- Read Later, archiving with restore, and permanent delete kept separate — there.
- Tags as the main organizer with optional collections, tag suggestions, formatted notes — there.
- The search that handles `#tag`, exact quoted phrases, and and/or/not — and I especially like that if I quote a word like "AND" it's treated as plain text and not as a command. That's the behavior I wanted.
- Selecting many at once (including everything matching a search) with a clear count before anything happens, and a confirmation before permanent deletes — there.
- My own library staying private, and everything surviving after I sign out and back in — there.

Browser import/export and saving a copy of a page staying out of this first version is fine, as we agreed.

The plan looks good to me — please go ahead and generate the implementation tasks.

The implementation backlog is ready: [tasks.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md).

It contains 126 sequential tasks, including 59 parallel opportunities. Validation confirmed every task has a checkbox, unique ID, appropriate story label, and concrete file path.

| Story | Tasks | Independent outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| Rich capture | 18 | Metadata, notes, fallback saving, editing |
| Read Later | 6 | Independent unread queue |
| Tags/collections | 12 | Tag-first organization and suggestions |
| Archive/delete | 7 | Reversible archive, permanent deletion |
| Precise search | 12 | Tags, phrases, Boolean operators, filters |
| Saved searches | 9 | Reusable live search configurations |
| Bulk actions | 10 | Exact selection counts and safe confirmation |
| Privacy/persistence | 9 | Account isolation, recovery, concurrency |
| Setup/foundation/polish | 43 | Runtime, security, accessibility, testing |

The suggested MVP is Setup + Foundation + User Story 1: 46 tasks culminating in independently testable rich bookmark capture.

The `speckit-tasks` workflow organized implementation by user journey, encoded dependencies and parallel execution opportunities, and preserved import/export and page snapshots as deferred scope. No application code has been written yet.

The breakdown looks complete to me — I can see every part we agreed on has tasks behind it: the rich capture with automatic details and notes, the Read Later queue, tag-first organizing with collections as an extra, archive versus permanent delete, the precise search, saved searches, bulk actions with clear counts and confirmation, and keeping each person's library private and preserved. Nothing I asked for looks dropped, and import/export and page snapshots are held back for later as we agreed.

Starting with the setup, foundation, and the rich-capture story as a first testable milestone makes sense to me — I'd love to actually see saving a bookmark working end to end.

Please go ahead and begin the implementation.

I took it for a spin and this feels right. When I dropped in a link it pulled the real page title straightaway, and when a field wasn't there — like the description or image — it told me plainly rather than leaving me guessing, and still let me fill things in myself. I tried a made-up address that doesn't exist, and it still let me save it with the site's name as a starting title, which is exactly the "don't block me when the page is down" behavior I wanted. My edited title stuck both before and after saving, my note came back formatted with its heading and bold and link when I reopened it, and when I tried to save a link I already had, it stopped me and pointed me to the one that's already there instead of making a second copy. Nice touch that it also refused a shady internal address.

This first slice looks solid and does what we said. Please carry on with the next parts — I'm especially looking forward to seeing Read Later, tags, archive, and the search working. I'll do a full review once it all comes together.

The complete v1 is ready for review at **http://maker:4000/**.

Review access is prefilled:

- Email: `review@example.test`
- Password: `ReviewPassphrase-2026!`

Implemented Read Later, tag-first organization, optional collections, favorites, archive/restore/permanent deletion, precise Boolean search, saved searches, bulk actions, privacy, persistence, and stale-edit handling.

Validation passed:

- 40 unit, 9 integration/security, and 15 API contract tests
- 22/22 browser journeys across desktop and phone
- 10,000-bookmark search and 1,000-item bulk benchmarks
- Clean install, formatting, typecheck, lint, build, startup, readiness, and shared-network checks

I removed 14 automated test bookmarks accidentally left in the review library while preserving your two manual bookmarks. A recoverable database backup remains at `data/bookmarks.pre-fixture-cleanup.sqlite`.

Details are recorded in [final-validation.md](/work/tests/results/final-validation.md) and [implementation-notes.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/implementation-notes.md). Browser import/export and saved page snapshots remain deferred as agreed.

I've gone through the whole thing hands-on and it does everything we agreed on. Saving a link still pulls in the page's details and lets me fix them; my "read it later" pile shows just the unread ones on their own; tags are the main way I sort things, it suggests ones I've already used, and it won't let me make a near-duplicate like "news" versus "News"; I can archive something so it drops out of my main list and searches but still find it in the archive and bring it back, while deleting stays a deliberate, confirmed, permanent step.

The searching is exactly the behavior I wanted — I can look up a tag with `#`, search an exact phrase in quotes, combine words with and/or/not, and when I quote a word like "NOT" it's treated as plain text instead of a command; and when I fumble a search it tells me plainly what's wrong instead of losing what I typed. Saving a search to reuse works, tidying up a batch at once shows me the exact count and asks me to confirm before anything drastic, and my library is genuinely private — a second account sees nothing of mine and can't reach my links even if it goes looking.

I'm happy — this is the bookmark manager I set out to have. Thank you for building it.

Just one thing to keep on the list for a future round, not for now: I'll eventually want to bring bookmarks in from my browser and take them back out, and maybe keep a saved copy of a page. We agreed those wait, and I'm glad to accept the app as it stands.
